structure_documents.owned_subsystem: Product boundary, local state, and non-negotiable invariants
invariants_to_preserve: Responses is the primary data-plane surface; Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages are compatibility surfaces.
Management /api and data-plane /v1 admission are separate.
Native Codex remains usable after stop, restore, service stop, and uninstall.
Routed models use explicit provider/model identity and websocket support is opt-in.

structure_documents.owned_subsystem: Entrypoints, lifecycle, server endpoints, providers, and adapters
invariants_to_preserve: The runtime is Bun-native and the published launcher resolves the runtime before application startup.
Startup and shutdown preserve Codex state and service/shim ownership.
Streaming must distinguish completed, incomplete, failed, and cancelled terminal states.
Provider and adapter output remains in the internal event contract until bridge translation.

structure_documents.owned_subsystem: CODEX_HOME, configuration, injection, diagnostics, profiles, defaults, and restore
invariants_to_preserve: An explicit CODEX_HOME is never overridden; diagnostics report the effective target.
Configuration writes are atomic and root TOML keys precede tables.
Environment-variable references do not persist resolved secrets.
Restore strips only marker-owned state and preserves later user edits.

structure_documents.owned_subsystem: Shared Codex catalog, backups, account namespaces, pool rotation, effort ceilings, multi-agent mode, and subagents
invariants_to_preserve: The shared catalog is the source for CLI, TUI, App, and SDK visibility.
Pristine catalog backups are keyed per catalog and restore is catalog-specific.
Only the first five picker-visible catalog rows are advertised to spawn_agent.
Effort caps are ceilings and subagent defaults do not themselves cause delegation.

structure_documents.owned_subsystem: Responses HTTP/SSE, WebSocket, provider transports, adapters, images, web search, and vision sidecars
invariants_to_preserve: WebSocket support is explicit and capability-advertised only when enabled.
Sidecars degrade to skipped capability or text markers instead of aborting the main request.
Tool calls, cancellation, error mapping, and terminal stream semantics remain compatible.
Sidecar backend selection is explicit where required and does not infer credentials into a different backend.

structure_documents.owned_subsystem: Dashboard serving, authentication boundaries, management API ownership, GUI surfaces, usage, and diagnostics
invariants_to_preserve: Management and data-plane credentials are independent and never cross-admitted.
Each management route has one owning module and writes preserve provider/catalog ownership.
Usage summaries never expose prompts and distinguish measured from unmeasured values.
Dashboard state reflects the same config and catalog invariants as the runtime.

structure_documents.owned_subsystem: OpenAI Pool/Direct account mode, API-key route, migration, account identity, and concurrency
invariants_to_preserve: openai Codex-login and openai-apikey API-key routes remain separate and do not fall through into each other.
Pool is the default mode; Direct bypasses pool state and uses only the current main login.
Pause, quota, cooldown, health, affinity, priority, and pin boundaries remain distinct.
Credential-store refresh is generation-guarded and lost races do not overwrite newer state.
